title: A field-linear projective-line automorphism preserves the degree-one twist
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field], let $q:P=\mathbf P^1_k\to\operatorname{Spec} k$ be the standard projective line [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], and let $\mathcal O_P(1)$ be its actual projective twist [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. If $a:P\simeq P$ is a scheme isomorphism with $q\circ a=q$, then $a^*\mathcal O_P(1)\simeq\mathcal O_P(1)$ as modules [def-sc-invertible-module]. There are no restrictions on the characteristic or algebraic closure of $k$.

source.place: Remark 4.2.7, printed p.75, field degree-one clause. The direct degree calculation uses Stacks Tag 0BXJ (divisors.tex, lemma-Pic-projective-space-UFD) and Tag 01XS (coherent.tex, section-cohomology-projective-space and lemma-cohomology-projective-space-over-ring).

proof.text: The pullback of the invertible O(1) is invertible. Apply the existing field classification to obtain an integer d and an isomorphism a*O(1) ≅ O(d). The standard twists satisfy TwistData by twistData in ProjectiveSpace.LineTwist.

The map a is an isomorphism over k. Pullback therefore preserves the k-vector space of global sections (the existing finrankH_pullback_of_isIso API). Consequently h0(O(d)) equals h0(O(1))=2. The monomial formula gives zero when d<0 and d+1 when d≥0. For d≥0 the monomials are indexed by exponents (d-j,j), 0≤j≤d, so the dimension is d+1 over every field.

The negative case contradicts 0=2. In the nonnegative case d+1=2 forces d=1. Substitute this into the classification isomorphism. No uniqueness of the classification degree or automorphism of the group Z is used.
